headline: Add Loans module for customer loan applications, annuity calculation, and officer approval or rejection.
summary: Introduces the Bank.Modules.Loans module with API endpoints, application service logic, domain entity, and database persistence for fixed-rate loans. Customers can apply for and view their loans, while loan officers can inspect, approve, and reject applications with ledger disbursement and event notifications.
business: Customers can apply for 6 to 120 month loans between 1000 and 50000 at a fixed 5.5% annual rate and receive decision notifications. Loan officers can review, approve with automatic principal disbursement to the customer account, or reject applications with a reason.

reasons.claim: ApproveAsync does not verify whether the approving officer is also the applicant (loan.CustomerId == officerId). This allows loan officers to approve their own loans and disburse funds to themselves, violating the four-eyes requirement and causing test failure.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add `if (loan.CustomerId == officerId) throw new UnauthorizedAccessException("Loan officers cannot approve their own loan.");` immediately after loading the loan.
reasons.say: Loan officers can approve their own loans and disburse bank funds to themselves, violating four-eyes controls. Ask the author to block self-approval in LoanService.ApproveAsync before sign-off.
reasons.say_facts: This allows loan officers to approve their own loans and disburse funds to themselves, violating the four-eyes requirement and causing test failure. Tests agree. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.text: Missing four-eyes check allows loan officers to approve their own loans
reasons.claim: ApproveAsync does not verify whether loan.CustomerId matches the caller's officerId before disbursing funds. A loan officer with a customer account can approve their own application and trigger unauthorized principal payout.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add `if (loan.CustomerId == officerId) throw new UnauthorizedAccessException("Loan officers cannot approve their own loan.");` prior to initiating disbursement.
reasons.say: A loan officer with a customer account can self-approve a loan and trigger unauthorized payout. Verify LoanService.ApproveAsync rejects approvals where the officer matches the borrower.
reasons.say_facts: A loan officer with a customer account can approve their own application and trigger unauthorized principal payout. Tests agree. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.text: Class-level Customer policy blocks LoanOfficer access to Approve and Reject endpoints
reasons.claim: In ASP.NET Core, authorization attributes combine additively. Placing [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] on the controller class forces all actions—including Approve and Reject—to require both Policies.Customer and Policies.LoanOfficer. Loan officers without the Customer role will receive 403 Forbidden, violating the API specification.
reasons.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the LoansController class and apply it directly to Apply and Get actions so Approve and Reject only require Policies.LoanOfficer.
reasons.evidence:
[ApiController]
[Route("api/loans")]
[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]
public sealed class LoansController : ControllerBase
reasons.say: Loan officers without customer permissions will be blocked from approving or rejecting loans. Ask the author to remove the class-level customer policy on LoansController so staff can review applications.
reasons.say_facts: Loan officers without the Customer role will receive 403 Forbidden, violating the API specification. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Static LoanLocks creates an unbounded memory leak and ineffective distributed synchronization
reasons.claim: LoanService stores SemaphoreSlim instances in a static ConcurrentDictionary keyed by loanId without any cleanup or eviction, leaking memory over the lifetime of the process. In-memory semaphores also fail to prevent concurrency races across multiple service instances in a distributed deployment.
reasons.suggested_fix: Remove the in-memory SemaphoreSlim dictionary and rely on database transactions and status checks (or a distributed lock if multi-node serialization is required).
reasons.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> LoanLocks = new();
reasons.say: Memory will leak over time as loans accumulate, and locks will fail across multiple servers, risking double payouts. Ask for database-level concurrency control instead of LoanLocks.
reasons.say_facts: In-memory semaphores also fail to prevent concurrency races across multiple service instances in a distributed deployment. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Class-level Customer policy on LoansController restricts LoanOfficer endpoints
reasons.claim: LoansController is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] at the class level. In ASP.NET Core, class-level and action-level authorization attributes combine, requiring callers of Approve and Reject to satisfy both Policies.Customer and Policies.LoanOfficer, which denies loan officers who do not also possess the Customer role.
reasons.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the controller class and place it specifically on the Apply and Get action methods.
reasons.evidence:
[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]
public sealed class LoansController : ControllerBase
reasons.say: Staff who are only loan officers will get access-denied errors when approving or rejecting loans. Ask the author to move the customer policy off the LoansController class to customer endpoints only.
reasons.say_facts: In ASP.NET Core, class-level and action-level authorization attributes combine, requiring callers of Approve and Reject to satisfy both Policies.Customer and Policies.LoanOfficer, which denies loan officers who do not also possess the Customer role. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Unbounded memory retention in static LoanLocks dictionary
reasons.claim: LoanLocks accumulates a SemaphoreSlim instance for every approved or rejected loan ID in a static ConcurrentDictionary without eviction or disposal. In a running service, this creates an unbounded memory leak as loan volume increases over time.
reasons.suggested_fix: Use database row-level locking or an entity concurrency token instead of an unbounded in-memory static semaphore dictionary, or remove keys when work completes.
reasons.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> LoanLocks = new();
reasons.say: Every approved or rejected loan permanently holds memory in LoanLocks, which can eventually crash the service. Ask the author to clean up or replace this static lock storage.
reasons.say_facts: In a running service, this creates an unbounded memory leak as loan volume increases over time. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Unbounded static dictionary for per-loan locks creates memory leak
reasons.claim: LoanLocks statically retains a SemaphoreSlim instance for every processed loanId without eviction or cleanup. In long-running service instances, this causes monotonically increasing memory consumption.
reasons.suggested_fix: Rely on database transactions with concurrency tokens/optimistic concurrency on the Loan entity, or remove entries from LoanLocks when locks are no longer in use.
reasons.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> LoanLocks = new();
reasons.say: Unbounded memory growth from LoanLocks will steadily degrade service stability in production. Confirm with the author how lock entries will be evicted or replaced with database locking.
reasons.say_facts: In long-running service instances, this causes monotonically increasing memory consumption. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: LoansController endpoints and status code translations lack test coverage
reasons.claim: LoansController introduces four HTTP endpoints (POST api/loans, GET api/loans/{id}, POST api/loans/{id}/approve, POST api/loans/{id}/reject), custom JSON body reading, and exception-to-HTTP-status mappings (400, 403, 404, 409). None of these actions or controller behaviors are covered by any unit or integration tests.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add controller unit tests or integration tests verifying routing, authorization policy enforcement, status code mappings, and request body deserialization for all four endpoints.
reasons.say: None of the loan web endpoints or error status responses are tested, risking broken customer or staff requests. Ask for integration tests covering LoansController endpoints and error codes.
reasons.say_facts: None of these actions or controller behaviors are covered by any unit or integration tests. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Loan domain entity invalid state transitions are not directly tested
reasons.claim: The acceptance criteria requires testing invalid state transitions, and the Loan domain entity defines Approve and Reject methods that validate Status == LoanStatus.Submitted. However, no tests execute Loan.Approve or Loan.Reject directly on the domain model to verify state transition guards independently of LoanService.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add domain unit tests verifying that calling Approve or Reject directly on a Loan instance that is already Disbursed or Rejected throws InvalidOperationException.
reasons.say: Invalid loan status transitions are not tested directly on the loan record, leaving state rules unverified. Ask for unit tests confirming invalid Loan approvals and rejections are blocked.
reasons.say_facts: However, no tests execute Loan.Approve or Loan.Reject directly on the domain model to verify state transition guards independently of LoanService. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: Annuity rounding test does not test midpoint rounding half-away-from-zero
reasons.claim: The test Apply_accepts_inclusive_boundaries_and_rounds_annuity_away_from_zero claims to verify that payments round half-away-from-zero, but none of the test cases calculate a monthly payment ending in a half-cent midpoint (.XX5). For the inputs tested (169.3496..., 858.374..., 542.628...), MidpointRounding.ToEven and MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero produce identical results, so the test would pass even if banker's rounding or default rounding were used.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add a test case with principal and term values where the third decimal digit of the calculated annuity is exactly 5, ensuring that AwayFromZero rounding behaves differently from default ToEven rounding.
reasons.evidence:
[Theory]
    [InlineData(1000, 6, 169.35)]
    [InlineData(10000, 12, 858.37)]
    [InlineData(50000, 120, 542.63)]
    public async Task Apply_accepts_inclusive_boundaries_and_rounds_annuity_away_from_zero(
        decimal principal, int termMonths, decimal expectedMonthlyPayment)
reasons.say: The rounding test does not check half-cent values, so incorrect rounding could miscalculate customer monthly payments. Ask for a test case whose exact payment ends in half a cent.
reasons.say_facts: For the inputs tested (169.3496..., 858.374..., 542.628...), MidpointRounding.ToEven and MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero produce identical results, so the test would pass even if banker's rounding or default rounding were used. Decide whether it must be fixed now.
